There's no shortage of AI tutorials, but most jump straight to calling an API or gloss over
*why* things work. This curriculum takes the opposite approach: build a **solid foundation**
that goes all the way from the base components of modern AI up to running models and agents
in production.

You start by understanding the building blocks — PyTorch, embeddings, transformers, training
loops — and progressively work up to fine-tuning, alignment, evaluation, retrieval, agents,
and LLMOps. Every topic is a short, self-contained, hands-on tutorial you can finish in about
**30 minutes a day**.

## What you'll learn

By the end you'll be able to:

- Understand transformers from the inside out — self-attention, RoPE, GQA, KV caching
- Build and train a small language model from scratch
- Fine-tune open models with modern pipelines (LoRA/QLoRA, Axolotl, Unsloth)
- Curate and generate training data, and align models with DPO/ORPO/SimPO
- Evaluate models rigorously (lm-eval-harness, LLM-as-judge) and track experiments
- Quantize, serve, and merge models (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF, vLLM, mergekit)
- Build RAG systems and AI agents
- Deploy, monitor, and secure LLM applications in production

## Format

- **120 tutorials**, one per day, ~30 minutes each
- Grouped into **24 sections of 5 tutorials**
- Ordered so each topic builds on the last — foundations first, no hand-waving

The learning arc:

**Foundations** → **Transformers & internals** → **Using LLMs** → **Fine-tuning track** →
**Applications (RAG & agents)** → **Production & capstone**

## Getting started

1. Skim the [full curriculum](sections/index.qmd) to see the whole roadmap.
2. Read [How to use](about.qmd) for setup and how each tutorial is structured.
3. Start at Section 1, Tutorial 1 — and do one a day.

::: {.callout-tip}
Each tutorial ends with **5 control questions** to self-test and **2 Python coding tasks**
you can open directly in Google Colab.
:::
